subject: Clarify geo-isolation guarantees & cross-region processing exceptions
messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@fintechco.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Amelia Hartwell <amlaw@clientlaw.com>, Procurement Team <procure@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-03-25 09:12 -0700
Subject: Geo-isolation question for EU production data

Mina / Redwood team,

Thanks for the product demo yesterday — FintechCo is excited about the latency profile. Before we move forward on a pilot we'd like written clarity on a few data residency items for EU customer data (GDPR scope):

- Can you confirm whether we can require that all production data for our account remain within EU regions at rest and in transit, including backups and snapshots?
- Are there any operational exceptions where data might cross to non-EU regions (e.g., failover during outages, debugging, analytics, or security investigations)? If so, what controls/approvals apply?
- Do you use customer-provided content for model improvements or training?
- Please attach your current DPA redline and a list of subprocessors (we need to run this through our security and procurement).

We're trying to decide between Redwood Hosted vs a Dedicated capacity commitment; the DPA/residency assurances are the gating factor for procurement.

Appreciate a concise summary and any sample contract language we can share with legal.

Best,
Olivia
Olivia Barnes
Head of Platform Partnerships
FintechCo

--
Attachment requests: DPA redline, subprocessors list, summary of SCCs or transfer mechanisms

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@fintechco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-25 11:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Geo-isolation question for EU production data

Olivia — thanks for the clear list. Summary up front: yes, we support EU-only residency guarantees but the exact commitment depends on the deployment mode. See short answer + attachments below.

Short answers:
- Dedicated & Private deployments: we can contractually pin data to EU regions (at-rest storage, backups, replication). That includes KMS keys kept in EU when configured and audit logs stored per-region.
- Hosted (shared): we offer region preference and best-effort routing to EU, and we offer a "region-lock" add-on for customers needing stronger guarantees, but hosted has narrow operational exceptions where cross-region processing may occur (failover, manual troubleshooting, or legal requirements). Those exceptions are documented in the DPA addendum.
- Cross-region exceptions: engineering diagnostics, ephemeral debug sandboxes, and aggregated analytics are the most common. We can require explicit customer approval for any extraction of identifiable payloads for debugging and provide redaction tools by default.
- Training: by default we DO NOT use customer-provided content to train or improve models for the hosted API. Any opt-in program is explicit and contractually separate.

Attachments included: redwood_dpa_addendum_v1.docx (proposed language for geo-isolation & exceptions), subprocessors_2026Q1.csv, SCCs_summary.pdf.

Next steps I propose:
1) I can run a short tech session with our infra/ops team to walk through what "failover" looks like operationally (how we route, TTLs, and how data may be replicated).
2) If your security team wants to redact certain fields before we ingest logs for debugging, we can provide an ingestion pipeline sample.
3) We'll provide a DocuSign-ready DPA addendum if you confirm the preferred deployment option (Hosted with add-on OR Dedicated).

Quick note from Aditya (cc'd) on technical limits: he can outline caching/replication behavior and KMS options.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior PM, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: redwood_dpa_addendum_v1.docx; subprocessors_2026Q1.csv; SCCs_summary.pdf

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@fintechco.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-26 08:27 -0700
Subject: Re: Geo-isolation question for EU production data

Hi Olivia — quick technical follow-up on what to expect from an infra perspective so your engineering team can evaluate risk.

- KV / prefix caches: these are kept in-region and are in-memory by default. For Dedicated deployments we can guarantee no asynchronous cross-region replication; for Hosted, we replicate metadata across regions for routing decisions but payloads are not routinely moved.
- Backups & snapshots: for Dedicated/Private we keep backups in EU storage buckets; for Hosted, backups are region-preferred but our disaster recovery playbooks may use alternate regions depending on the outage severity. We can agree on a maximum RPO and escalation route in the DPA addendum.
- Debugging support: when we need to reproduce a customer issue, Engineering may request a snapshot of the request/response; that snapshot can be sanitized locally (PII redaction) or hosted in a customer-controlled S3/GCS bucket if you prefer. We require a documented authorization (ticket + named approver) for any extraction.
- KMS & key locality: we support customer-managed keys (CMK) with cloud KMS providers; if you keep the keys in an EU KMS, any decryption for ops will also be constrained to EU.

We won't use customer content for model training unless explicitly opted into. Also, audit logs (who accessed what) can be retained in-region per retention terms.

If useful, I can prep a short appendix that describes the exact technical triggers that would allow cross-region processing (e.g., region down, DR invoked, manual debug with approval).

Cheers,
Sergio
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment referenced: subprocessors_2026Q1.csv

From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@fintechco.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Amelia Hartwell <amlaw@clientlaw.com>, Procurement Team <procure@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-03-29 10:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Geo-isolation question for EU production data

Thanks Mina / Sergio — that helps. A couple of clarifying points from legal/procurement:

- Debugging/triage policy: we need firm contract language that says Redwood will not copy or retain customer payloads outside EU except with prior written consent and that any debug artifacts will be redacted unless we expressly permit otherwise. Can you point to the clause in the DPA addendum that covers this or provide specific suggested wording?
- Subprocessor escrow: we need the subprocessors file but also a 30-day notice for adding any new EU-located subprocessors that will process customer production data. Is that something Redwood can commit to?
- Cross-border lawful access: if Redwood receives a non-EU legal request for data belonging to our EU tenant, what is the decision process and notification timeline?

If we can get these three items captured in a DPA addendum, Procurement is willing to move to a pilot (Hosted with the geo-lock add-on for initial rollout). Otherwise we'll need to pursue Dedicated.

Also Amelia (copied) had a quick question on training: we appreciate the "opt-in" statement, but we need it in writing that customer content will not be used for model improvements unless we sign a separate agreement.

Best,
Olivia

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@fintechco.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-30 15:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Geo-isolation question for EU production data

Olivia / Amelia — thanks for the close read. A few commitments we can make now and proposed contract language below.

Commitments:
1) Data locality: "For customers electing an EU geo-isolation option (Hosted w/ geo-lock add-on, Dedicated, or Private), Redwood shall ensure that production application payloads, backups, and snapshots are stored and processed within the European Economic Area, except as expressly permitted in Section 3 (Operational Exceptions)."

2) Operational Exceptions: "Operational Exceptions include (a) disaster recovery where documented DR playbooks are invoked; (b) emergency debugging with prior written customer authorization; (c) where decryption is necessary to respond to a lawful request and Redwood is legally compelled to comply. Any Operational Exception that results in cross-border transfer of customer payloads will be documented and notification provided to the customer within 72 hours, unless prohibited by law."

3) Subprocessor notice: "Redwood will provide 30 days' prior written notice before adding any subprocessor that will process production payloads for EU-geolocked customers. For changes classified as urgent (e.g., security patching), Redwood will provide notice as soon as practicable and will allow customers to object and request reasonable mitigations."

4) Model training: "Redwood will not use customer-provided content for model training, fine-tuning, or improvements absent an explicit, documented, and signed opt-in agreement."

We will incorporate the above terms into the DPA addendum and circulate a DocuSign package for signature. Link: https://www.docusign.net/transaction/ABC123

Operational note: for Hosted with geo-lock we will also enable an audit trail and a named approver workflow for any debug extraction; for Dedicated/Private those workflows are configurable to your processes.

If this matches what your legal/procurement need, say 'approved' here and I'll get the DocuSign out to your procurement contact and attach a redline showing the exact clause locations.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Ops (acting)
Redwood Inference
